content.value_statement: Research teams need repeatable ways to turn datasets and papers into testable hypotheses. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Hypogenic setup, configuration, generation, inference, and evaluation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation of the Hypogenic package and example datasets.
Explains dataset formats for training, validation, and test splits.
Shows configuration templates for hypothesis generation and inference prompts.
Describes HypoGeniC, HypoRefine, and Union workflows.
Provides CLI and Python API examples for generating and testing hypotheses.
Documents literature processing with GROBID for paper-based workflows.
limitations: It does not include the Hypogenic package source code.
It requires external packages, datasets, and optional GROBID services.
Generated hypotheses need expert review before scientific use.
Performance depends on dataset quality, labels, prompts, and selected language model.

use_cases.title: Explore New Research Datasets
use_cases.description: Generate candidate hypotheses from labeled observational data before deeper statistical analysis.

use_cases.title: Blend Papers with Empirical Data
use_cases.description: Use HypoRefine to combine literature insights with validation data for theory-grounded hypotheses.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Competing Explanations
use_cases.description: Run inference across hypothesis banks to compare which explanations fit held-out examples.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a First Hypothesis Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Hypogenic to create 20 data-driven hypotheses for my labeled dataset. Review the required file format and outline the setup steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Test Generated Hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hypogenic_inference to test my saved hypothesis bank against a test split. Summarize the expected inputs and evaluation outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Literature and Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a HypoRefine workflow for ten research papers and my validation data. Include PDF preprocessing, configuration needs, and comparison steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Custom Research Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a custom Hypogenic task with prompt templates, label extraction rules, caching, and a repeatable evaluation workflow.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced customization for a domain-specific task.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for a data-driven workflow for AI-generated text detection.
output_examples.output: The skill returns setup steps, dataset requirements, configuration guidance, generation options, and testing steps for a HypoGeniC workflow.

output_examples.input: A team wants to compare literature-only and data-driven hypotheses.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines HypoRefine and Union methods, paper preprocessing needs, hypothesis banks, and evaluation comparisons.

output_examples.input: A user needs help parsing model predictions for accuracy scoring.
output_examples.output: The skill explains custom label extraction and reminds the user to align prediction labels with dataset labels.

best_practices: Review every generated hypothesis with a domain expert before reporting results.
Use held-out test data and record model, prompt, and configuration choices.
Inspect external packages and cloned repositories before running setup commands.
anti_patterns: Treating generated hypotheses as scientific conclusions without validation.
Mixing training and test examples during hypothesis generation.
Running external setup scripts without checking their source and permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps configure Hypogenic workflows for generating, refining, and testing scientific hypotheses with language models.

faq.question: Does it create final scientific claims?
faq.answer: No. It creates candidate hypotheses that require validation, expert review, and careful reporting.

faq.question: Can it use research papers?
faq.answer: Yes. The HypoRefine workflow processes papers with GROBID and combines literature insights with empirical data.

faq.question: Does it need API keys?
faq.answer: Hypogenic can use API-based models, so users may need provider credentials. Store keys in environment variables, not configuration files.

faq.question: Can I use local models?
faq.answer: The skill describes support for local LLMs when the Hypogenic environment is configured for them.

faq.question: What should I check before running commands?
faq.answer: Review package versions, cloned repositories, setup scripts, and dataset licenses before executing external tools.
